citation.sourceDocument: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 AMT exemption & thresholds); IRC §55 (26%/28% rates)
citation.sourceNote: The alternative minimum tax runs a parallel calculation: a flat 26% on the first slice of alternative minimum taxable income and 28% above it, against an exemption that itself phases out for high earners. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.10 gives the 2026 exemptions — $140,200 joint or surviving spouse, $90,100 unmarried, $70,100 married filing separately — and the 28%-rate threshold, $244,500 for everyone except married filing separately at $122,250 (exactly half). The exemption phases out at 25 cents per dollar of AMTI above $1,000,000 joint and $500,000 for all other statuses, including married filing separately, which is NOT half here — an asymmetry worth stating because the 28% threshold two lines above it IS halved. This shard drives a screener, not a filing calculation. Omitted: the AMT credit for prior-year AMT paid, the separate kiddie-tax exemption under §59(j), the preferential capital-gains rates inside the AMT computation, and the long list of adjustments and preferences (incentive stock option spreads, private-activity bond interest, depletion) that make real AMTI differ from taxable income. The screener says whether AMT is worth investigating, not what it would be. Verified against Rev. Proc. 2025-32 on 2026-08-29.
